how: Recruitment takes the minimal form of calls to build logos and emotes or recover an image, with uptake left unresolved.
Proposers occupy the starter role at its unanswered-request end without establishing that others joined their work.
An attempted recolouring ends with a participant concluding that it will not work.
Being squeezed out leads a participant to cut losses after an attempt sustained since the previous day.
Crowding supports abandonment and consideration of alternatives, but neither suggested space nor discovery elsewhere establishes that the original builders moved.
Giving up the crowded attempt is a supported endpoint that must remain distinct from relocating or starting again.

statement: Explaining the canvas can be a self-contained exchange without recruiting participants.
how: Questions elicit an enthusiastic description, renewed confusion, a familiar comparison, and an article without a recorded commitment to place.
The preserved canvas reply sequences show a rule warning, feasibility assessment, and conditional repair offer rather than a bare commitment to join.
Preserved replies do not establish bare joining, while acceptance through silent placing remains outside the evidence.
A participant attempts to revise the logo from black to white without establishing collective agreement over the design.
A proposed Kappa location and colour plan show representation at the proposal end of the model's range.
Participants circulate a project template, locate an existing image, and offer another template for repair.
Template circulation does not establish design agreement when the surviving words offer alternatives and conditional repair rather than a settled instruction.
Reporting an existing image's coordinates establishes its reported presence without attributing construction to the room or its earlier callers.
Finding an existing image can elicit a repair-template offer before the record establishes any construction by the room.
Calls and a later report of an existing image do not identify who built it or link its construction to recruitment.
The cited templates do not establish scripts, bots, or spare accounts placing pixels.
Individual proposals and template sharing cannot establish whether the room did or did not decide its organisational order.
Recovery calls and repair offers establish intended upkeep while leaving performed repair and sustained defence unobserved.
An existing image and a conditional repair offer do not establish a locally built mark followed by performed upkeep.
Descriptions of takeover and crowding leave the responsible placers and their intentions unidentified.
An incoming advocate identifies a threatened tree, defends its value, and appeals to builders to spare it and allow regrowth.
A visitor speaks for a named neighbouring group and carries a preservation appeal without proving authorisation or receiving an observed agreement.
A participant rules out desired relocation because it would destroy other artwork.
The stated cost of killing existing artwork constrains where the image should move, independently of any demonstrated treaty or attack call.
A preservation appeal establishes a request for restraint without a preserved border agreement, truce, or deal.
Abandoning an attempt, suggesting quieter space, and finding another image do not establish an executed relocation.
The visitor requests non-destruction without documenting traded labour or a reciprocal pixel bargain.
A visitor and an externally hosted template do not establish coalition membership or joint organisation.
Locating the tree within the meme area shows overlap without establishing host permission or a guest arrangement.
Speaking for a group is preserved, but the record supplies no dispute over authority to bind that group.
The incoming appeal establishes neither an agreement nor a subsequent challenge to who can commit the room.
Proposing familiar emotes does not establish carried-in ideology, collective politics, or allegiance to a colour faction.
A proposed overlapping location and refusal to destroy artwork do not establish a pre-existing quarrel carried into the canvas.
The proposed site and later restraint do not supply an attack turn that names a rival through a prior tie.
An automated body-rule removal and a participant's approval warning constrain canvas recruitment within the host's posting rules.
Rule enforcement after recruitment does not warrant a flood mechanism when the explicit reasons concern body format and prior moderator approval.
Reactions to an external platform prank establish a local joke dispute without establishing host-wide parody or a joking frame for canvas calls.

statement: Members negotiate whether to remove or tolerate an external platform's April Fools prank.
how: A removal request receives agreement, advice to wait, and an instruction to take a joke, independently of canvas organising.

statement: Participants question whether another member's repeated posting serves an ambition to become a moderator.
how: The accusation remains a distinct local interaction whose deleted antecedent prevents attributing actual rule enforcement or an appointment.

statement: Members evaluate how much streaming coverage the canvas receives.
how: The surviving one-stream claim records perceived coverage scarcity while its explanatory replies leave the numerical claim unverified.
Finding an image and proposing repair do not establish completion celebration or collective credit.
Project and repair templates are prospective aids rather than evidence of preserving a final record.
Repair proposals and discussion of streaming coverage do not establish a successor purpose or continuation beyond the event.
The available pre-close concepts cannot test a post-close dispute about which version of the canvas or event should be kept.
Proposing a site over named areas does not establish an executed attack or an explicit call to deface a rival.
The preserved accusation concerns a member's supposed moderator ambition rather than a contest carried on with a named rival room.
Recruitment and a proposed overlapping location do not establish a subsequent attack, while a later participant expressly objects to destroying artwork.
Restraint is justified by prospective harm to artwork without a preserved preceding attack call to which it constitutes refusal.
